title: From dancing to a band, drums and then piano
summary: The dance trio played matinees, then formed a band; he filled in on drums, then switched to piano with help from Father Tux and blues pianist Sullivan Rock.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: You know you used to dance at the matinees.
That's why I picked a little hype. You know, the bands at the land of the air. And all the schools used to go to the matinees.

Yeah. And until we sat down one day, we said we're going to make some real money. We're going to get a band. We did. We got out of Bama. Big Bama. We played trumpet. That's his father Tux I was telling you about. He was his piano player. And Charlie up here would drink so much. His brother Junior was on the drums. We had no bass player at that time. And when everything was over with, that music just stayed in me. For some reason I knew around and I drift back to Junior's drums. One night Junior was sick and I had to play drums in his place. And Father Tux liked it in the way I played the drums. He said, you really got a good beat. You ought to try to be a musician. He said, you just, I said, well if I can get me a set of drums I just might play drums because I was getting tired of dancing. You know. But I really wanted to play music but I learned how to dance. I said, all right, I managed to scuffle up to get a piece of drums here, head there. Then I got both of them, it got monogamous, a toting drum, nobody give you a hand. You can toot all your own stuff. I said, I don't think I'm going to fool with those drums. He played too well not to play something. When he said something I said, you think I can lay down and play piano? I ain't got to tote nothing. I was already there. I was playing on you. He said, I don't know, I'll help you. So he did and started off with me and I was doing so good. Sullivan Rock walked in and he was a blues piano player. He said, come on boy, let me show you how to play the fine top of the woodwork so you would have something to play. But you ain't, they would always kick one another by different, you know, one another's music, all one figured they'd play better than the other. And when he said that, well that's what I really wanted to learn anyhow, cause a brother Montgomery was a friend of mine and he was really the composer of fine top boogie wood. And Rocky Sullivan would play as good as he could. We all call him Rocky Sullivan from that picture but his name was Sullivan Rock. Song
